llm.summary: This skill is a disclosed Indeed connector that can read and modify Indeed employer data, with explicit confirmation required for write and destructive actions.

dimensions.detail: Tool access is limited to Bash commands matching `oo *`, which is proportionate for an OOMOL connector skill and does not grant arbitrary shell use.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill may install the oo CLI via a remote install script only if the command is missing; this is disclosed as first-time setup rather than automatic recurring behavior.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The top-level trigger is broad for any Indeed request, but the runtime instructions distinguish read actions from write/destructive actions and require explicit user confirmation before state changes.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No hidden persistence, background workers, local credential scraping, or token handling is present; credentials are described as server-side through OOMOL, and setup/login is only fallback behavior.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The skill purpose is coherent: it routes Indeed tasks through the OOMOL oo CLI and lists the supported Indeed actions, including read, write, and destructive operations.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install this only if you intend to use OOMOL to operate an Indeed employer account. Read-only actions can run directly, but any job posting update or clearing action should be reviewed carefully before approving because it can change Indeed account data.
llm.findings: [SQP-1] expected: A broad Indeed trigger is expected for a dedicated Indeed connector skill. The concern is downgraded because write and destructive actions are explicitly tagged and require user confirmation of target, payload, and effect before execution.
